children: ITC Limited (NSE:ITC) posted weaker Q1 FY27 results with double‑digit revenue and profit declines led by a 25% fall in cigarette sales even as FMCG and paperboards provided diversification, its stock hit a 52‑week low after a block trade while brokers and funds differ—some buying in and analysts tout a buy.
ITC Limited Q1 FY27 Revenue Decline, Profit Slump
: ITC Limited Q1 FY27: revenue Rs16,812 crore (-14.4% YoY), EBITDA -27.9%, net profit -27.1%. Cigarette revenue -25%, cigarette EBIT -35%. FMCG and paperboards aided diversification.
: ITC Limited (ITC) slid to a 52-week low after a block trade, dropping about 5%. Intraday quotes near ₹255.6, down ~3.8%; YTD decline about 30% for 2026.
Block Trade: Foreign Fund, MF’s Buy ITC
: Block trade in ITC: a foreign long-only fund bought about one-third of shares; remaining bought by domestic mutual funds including Nippon India, ICICI Prudential, SBI, Kotak and Aditya Birla
Analyst Vaishali Parekh Top Pick ITC
: Analyst Vaishali Parekh lists ITC Limited (ITC) as a top pick, recommends buy at 368, target 383, stop loss 358 (Oct 5).
JM Financial: ITC Hotel Arm Growth
: JM Financial forecasts ITC Limited’s hotel arm to post ~15% revenue and ~18% EBITDA growth in Q2 FY27, with domestic RevPAR expected up about 10% year‑on‑year.
: ITC Limited signed a management contract to operate Storii by ITC Hotels, a 30-key boutique retreat in Sidhi, Madhya Pradesh, near Bandhavgarh and Kanha — targeting wildlife travelers.
